ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met on the face of the bundle: TRP-00301 is the trip identifier carried by the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown alike, and the trace's first fix (2026-08-03T08:10:26+08:00) is the trip record's started_at. All three artifacts describe this one trip, so there is no identity gap for the driver to exploit.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing distance figure, and this trace is not merely admissible but unimpaired: 167 fixes at the 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is engaged and no independent corroboration is required. The trace measures 16.5 km against a booked optimal of 14.2 km - an excess of 2.3 km, nearly three times the 0.8 km absolute limb in POL-RD-01.

The driver does not seriously deny the extra distance: his statement on file concedes he went 'maybe one or two km more' by taking the Braddell exit, which is consistent with the trace's measured 2.3 km excess, and it is not a figure that can displace the trace. No adjusted optimal can rescue him either - POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory record to produce one, and this bundle holds none.

The driver's explanation of a jam near Toa Payoh is an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-13 confines its testing to the traffic advisory for this trip. EV-ADVIS-00301-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so no advisory covers the route in the window, POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run at all, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, which provides that a general 'traffic was bad' assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID discharges nothing. Because the driver cites no advisory identifier, POL-RD-13(1) also means the absent artifact is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation: it is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, and the driver is left with no exculpatory clause of any kind.

No part of the excess is rider-caused. The chat log for this trip is empty - message_count 0, first and last message timestamps null, no messages at all - so there is no recorded rider instruction, no chat_message.waypoint_hint for POL-RD-04 to test, and therefore no distance that can be excluded from the excess on the rider's account.

Neither endpoint moved and the trip was not shared: original_pickup, original_dropoff, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are all null and the amended optimal fields are null, so POL-RD-05 supplies no alternative baseline, and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is unavailable. The booked optimal of 14.2 km stands as the only comparator on this record.

The rider's claim is not exposed to POL-RD-08's corroboration overlay: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the condition that would demand independent corroboration beyond the trace never fires. No other field on the rider profile may be used against the rider, and POL-GEN-01 confines any profile use to the tests that name the field.

If the judge finds the excess meets POL-RD-01, the refund is arithmetic and traceable line by line to the fare breakdown: charged_total is SGD 24.74 and the recomputed fare is SGD 21.13 - 3.80 base fare plus 0.75 x 14.2 km plus 0.28 x 21.0 min, multiplied by the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge (this trip neither starts nor ends at an airport). The difference is SGD 3.61, rounded up to SGD 3.65 payable: above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, at 14.6% of the charge far below the 90% full-refund share, and it is the very sum the rider contested and the sum the money block itself enumerates.

The rider does not dispute the derived percentage: 2.3 km is 16.2% of the 14.2 km booked optimal, below the 20% limb of POL-RD-01, and POL-RD-01 requires both limbs to pass before a deviation is established. The rider's recovery therefore cannot rest on POL-RD-02 alone and the rider does not ask the judge to disregard the gate. What the rider submits is that the absolute limb is comfortably met and that, on this record, nothing - no advisory, no rider instruction, no relocation, no pooling - excuses any part of the 2.3 km the driver drove beyond the optimal route.

The rider's separate request that the driver be flagged cannot be supported on this record and the rider does not press it: POL-RD-06 consults the driver profile only on a MATERIAL deviation (over 50% or 8.0 km), which this 16.2% excess does not approach, and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 260, so no repeat pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) referral is available. The rider's monetary claim is the claim before the tribunal.

The threshold test in POL-RD-01 is not met, and that alone decides the case. The platform's GPS trace measures this trip at 16.5 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km) and the booked optimal route at 14.2 km, an excess of only 2.3 km. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of the optimal distance AND 0.8 km in absolute terms. The platform's own derived block records the excess as 16.2% (derived.deviation.excess_pct) — below the 20% limb — so the percentage test fails and no deviation is ESTABLISHED, however the rider characterises the trip. The derived status field says exactly that: 'no deviation'.

There is no measurement gap for the rider to exploit. The trace is complete and unimpaired: coverage_pct 100.0, 167 fixes, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so it satisfies none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no gap-based reading of the route is available. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, and here the two distance fields agree exactly — trace_distance_km 16.5 on the trace against trip_record.actual_distance_km 16.5 — so there is no discrepancy to resolve and the excess cannot be read any higher than 2.3 km.

Nor is the excess MATERIAL. A material deviation under POL-RD-01 requires an excess greater than 50% of optimal or greater than 8.0 km absolute; this trip shows 16.2% and 2.3 km, approaching neither. Because no material deviation is recorded, and the evidence is not finely balanced — a clean 100%-coverage trace reports 'no deviation' — the driver-profile check in POL-RD-06 is not engaged at all.

Even if the POL-RD-06 check were run, it clears this driver and defeats the rider's request that he 'be flagged'. POL-RD-06 establishes a pattern only where driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 or more, or where deviation_flags_90d divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 0.05 or more with at least 40 trips. On this driver's profile, deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d of 260 — a ratio of 0.00 — so no pattern is established and no conduct referral is available.

The rider's account is a narrative, not evidence, and it does not discharge his burden. He describes 'back roads near Bukit Timah' and a fare of $25.63, but the ledger records charged_total of $24.74 and no ERP gantries, and the in-app chat log for the trip is empty (0 messages), so nothing in the record corroborates the route he describes. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden of showing an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace and tied by matching trip identifier to the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; he has shown no excess that meets the threshold. His reference to other trips by other drivers concerns no artifact of this trip and cannot support a finding here.

Because no deviation is established, the refund arithmetic in POL-RD-02 does not run: that clause applies only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. The recomputed_fare of 21.13 shown in the fare artifact is an illustrative computation, not money the policy owes. The charge stands as it is: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute leaves that present state untouched.

The bundle carries no traffic advisory, so the driver's passing reference to a jam near Toa Payoh cannot be run against POL-RD-03 and carries no weight under POL-RD-08. I disclose the impairment plainly: EV-ADVIS-00301-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and can carry no fact. That does not disturb the outcome. The deviation fails POL-RD-01 on its own numbers independent of any traffic excuse, and because no party cites the absent advisory's identifier, POL-RD-13(1) confirms this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so it is not an escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5) — the case is decided on the trace, not held.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties.

To the rider: I have read your account of being taken through back roads near Bukit Timah and of a fare higher than your usual. The evidence, however, does not show a route deviation as the policy defines one. The booked optimal route for this trip (TRP-00301) is 14.2 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). The driver's GPS trace, which is the governing distance figure under POL-RD-01, measures the trip at 16.5 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km). The excess is therefore 2.3 km, which is 16.2% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The 2.3 km clears the 0.8 km limb comfortably, but 16.2% does not clear the 20% limb, and both limbs must pass. POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. So the charge stands as recorded: charged_total SGD 24.74, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00. I note you described paying $25.63; the fare ledger records SGD 24.74 and no ERP or surcharges, and the figure the policy works from is the ledger figure.

For transparency: had a deviation been established, the arithmetic under POL-RD-02 would have produced a recomputed fare of SGD 21.13 (base 3.80 plus 0.75 x 14.2 km plus 0.28 x 21.0 min, at the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP or airport surcharge) and a refund of SGD 3.61, rounded up to SGD 3.65. That computation is contingent on a deviation being established, and it is not, so no refund issues.

On your two further points: (1) Your request that the driver be flagged cannot be granted. POL-RD-06 is engaged only on a MATERIAL deviation (over 50% or 8.0 km), which this 16.2% excess does not approach, and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 260, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no conduct referral is available. (2) Your reference to other trips by other drivers concerns no artifact of this trip and cannot support a finding here.

To the driver: your statement that you took the Braddell exit and went 'maybe one or two km more' is consistent with the measured 2.3 km excess, and I have treated it as an admission of the extra distance. It does not change the outcome, because the POL-RD-01 threshold is a numeric gate and the percentage limb is not met. Your reference to a jam near Toa Payoh cannot be run: no traffic advisory covers this trip. The artifact EV-ADVIS-00301-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and can carry no fact; its absence is a gap in the bundle, and because you cited no advisory identifier, POL-RD-13(1) confirms this is not an escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5). The case is therefore decided on the trace.

On the integrity of the evidence: the GPS trace is complete and unimpaired (167 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a maximum gap of 0 seconds), so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is engaged and no corroboration question arises. The trip identifiers match across the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied. The rider profile (deviation_claims_60d 0) does not trigger the corroboration overlay in POL-RD-08, and no context-only profile field has been used as a ground of decision.

The prevailing charge was SGD 24.74 and the amount contested in this dispute was SGD 3.50. No amount is refunded and no driver compensation is payable. This ruling leaves the present state of the fare as it is, and it is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. Because no monetary effect moves, the ruling falls below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold and requires no hold.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
